“And he exerciseth all the power of the first beast before him, and causeth the earth and them which dwell therein to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.” The first beast was Rome. You may think nobody worships Rome today. Really?

Look at the days of the week. Sunday is the sun, Monday the moon, Tuesday Mars, Wednesday Mercury, Thursday Jupiter, Friday Venus and Saturday Saturn. Now the months: January is named after the Roman god Janus, with two faces looking to the future and the past. February comes from Februalia, a Roman festival of purification and atonement. March is Mars, the Roman god of war. April comes from aperire, to open, like flowers in spring. May is the goddess Maia, June is the goddess Juno. July was Quintilis, the fifth month, until Julius Caesar named it after his family, and August was Sextilis until the emperor Augustus named it after himself. September, October, November and December come from the Latin for seven, eight, nine and ten, so December still says it is the tenth month while it is counted as the twelfth.
